flashcard_questions.q: How many pairs of chromosomes are in a human body cell?
What type of cell division is mitosis?
flashcard_questions.a: Division producing two genetically identical daughter cells from one parent cell.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens to the DNA before a cell divides?
flashcard_questions.a: It replicates, so each chromosome is copied.

flashcard_questions.q: During mitosis, what happens to the two sets of chromosomes?
flashcard_questions.a: One set is pulled to each end of the cell.
An undifferentiated cell that can divide to produce more cells of the same type.

flashcard_questions.q: Which stem cells can differentiate into almost any type of human cell?
Where in the human body are adult stem cells found?
Which plant tissue contains stem cells that form any type of plant cell?
What is diffusion of particles in a gas or a solution?
flashcard_questions.a: The net movement of particles from higher to lower concentration.

flashcard_questions.q: Three factors affect diffusion rate: temperature, surface area, and the ____ ____.
Why do multicellular organisms need specialised exchange surfaces?
flashcard_questions.a: Their surface area to volume ratio is too small for diffusion alone.

flashcard_questions.q: What is osmosis in terms of water movement?
flashcard_questions.a: Diffusion of water from a dilute to a concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane.

flashcard_questions.q: In the osmosis practical, what happens to potato mass in a concentrated solution?
flashcard_questions.a: It falls, because water leaves the cells.

flashcard_questions.q: In which direction does active transport move substances?
flashcard_questions.a: Against the concentration gradient, from dilute to concentrated.

flashcard_questions.q: Where does the energy for active transport come from?

notes: 15 cards: 4 term→definition (mitosis, stem cell, diffusion, osmosis), 1 cloze on the diffusion rate factors, 3 structure→function/location (chromosome number, adult stem cells, meristem), 3 process-order cards (DNA replication, chromosome separation, active transport direction), 1 practical-to-outcome card from the osmosis required practical, 3 causal cards. Dropped the stem cell ethics discussion (not self-gradable), therapeutic cloning and the gut sugar example to stay inside 15; the lesson states the individual mitosis phases are not required, so no prophase/metaphase cloze.
